title: The Team That Never Quit
summary: An underdog school handball team loses every game early in the season, but by practicing hard and supporting each other instead of giving up, they finally pull off a surprising win against the league's strongest team.
poll: A team that never gives up will eventually succeed, no matter how many times it loses.

versions.title: The Team That Never Quit
versions.text:
Omar's team lost every game. They were the Falcons. They played handball at school.

Omar felt sad. His team tried hard. But they still lost each time.

Coach Faisal did not get mad. He said, "Keep trying. Do not give up." The team kept coming to practice.

Each week, they got a little better. They passed the ball well. They helped each other.

One day, a strong team came. The team was called the Hawks. The Hawks had won every game.

The Falcons played their best game yet. They passed well. They did not give up.

Near the end, Omar scored a goal. The Falcons won the game! Everyone cheered loud.

Omar felt proud of his team. They had never quit. That was what mattered most.

versions.title: The Team That Never Quit
versions.text:
Picture losing every single game of a season, one after another, with no end in sight. That is exactly what happened to Omar's school handball team, the Falcons, at the start of the year.

Omar felt sad after each discouraging loss. His teammates tried hard every time, but somehow they still lost each game by the final whistle.

Coach Faisal never got angry about their effort or the losses. Instead, he always said, "Keep trying. Never give up on each other." The whole team kept returning to practice, week after week, without complaint.

Slowly, the team began to improve. They passed the ball more smoothly, and their teamwork grew stronger as they encouraged each other at every practice.

One afternoon, a remarkably strong team arrived to play them. That team, called the Hawks, had won every single game they had played that entire year.

The Falcons played their best game of the whole season that day. They passed the ball well and kept supporting one another, even when the score felt discouraging.

Near the very end of the game, Omar scored an important goal. The Falcons won by just one point, and everyone on the team cheered with real delight.

Omar felt incredibly proud of his whole team. They had never once quit, and in the end, that was what mattered the most.

versions.title: The Team That Never Quit
versions.text:
Few beginnings feel more discouraging than losing every single game of a season, one after another, with seemingly no end in sight. That is precisely what happened to Omar's school handball team, the Falcons, widely regarded as the underdog of their entire league that year.

Omar felt genuinely discouraged after each defeat, and so did every one of his teammates. They tried hard each time, yet they still lost game after game by the final whistle, week after frustrating week, until losing nearly began to feel routine.

Coach Faisal never grew angry about the losses, however frustrating they became. Instead, he consistently reminded them, "Keep trying. Never give up on each other." The entire team kept returning to practice, week after week, without a single complaint.

Gradually, the team began to improve, even though the losses persisted for longer than anyone had hoped. They passed the ball more smoothly, and their teamwork grew noticeably stronger as genuine camaraderie developed among teammates who refused to blame one another.

One afternoon, a remarkably strong team arrived to play them. That team, known as the Hawks, had won every single game they had played that entire year, and nobody expected the Falcons to stand any real chance against them.

The Falcons played the finest game of their entire season that day, passing skillfully and supporting one another even when the score grew discouraging early on.

Near the very end of the match, Omar scored a decisive, game-changing goal that nobody inside the gymnasium had anticipated. The Falcons triumphed by a single point, and the entire team erupted in genuine delight.

Omar felt an overwhelming sense of pride in his teammates. Their resilience and perseverance throughout the hardest weeks of losing, he realized, mattered considerably more than any single victory ever could.

questions.why: The Falcons lose repeatedly at first, but steady practice and teamwork make them strong enough to beat the league's best team by the end.

wrong.A: The article clearly shows the team changing and improving.
wrong.B: The team's play gets better, not worse, over the season.
wrong.D: The Falcons specifically defeat the Hawks, their toughest opponent.

questions.stem: Why does the author describe the Falcons' effort continuing for many weeks before any success came?
options: To show that real improvement often takes sustained effort, not a quick fix
To explain the official rules of school handball in detail and the score of each game
To describe what the weather was like that season on the court, with rain and wind
To suggest that practice does not really help a team, and luck decides who wins
questions.why: Spreading the Falcons' effort across many difficult weeks shows that their eventual success came from sustained practice, not luck.

wrong.B: Handball's official rules are not explained in the article.
wrong.C: Weather is not described in the article.
wrong.D: The article shows practice clearly helping the team improve.

MID.prompt: Explain how the Falcons' teamwork and effort changed from the start of the season to the final game. Use at least two details from the article.
checklist: I explained how the team's teamwork and effort changed.
I used at least two details from the article.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: At the start of the season, the Falcons lost every game, but they kept returning to practice instead of quitting. Over the weeks, their teamwork grew stronger as they encouraged each other instead of blaming one another for mistakes. By the time they faced the undefeated Hawks, their steady effort and support for each other had made them strong enough to win the game by a single point.

keyWords.definition: continued effort to do or achieve something despite difficulty
keyWords.example: Her perseverance through months of rehabilitation eventually paid off.

keyWords.definition: a competitor who is expected to lose, with little chance of winning
keyWords.example: The small school was the underdog against the much larger team.

keyWords.definition: the ability to recover quickly from difficulty and keep going
keyWords.example: The firefighters admired the resilience of the family after the flood.

keyWords.definition: a feeling of friendship and trust among people who share experiences together
keyWords.example: Years of traveling together built real camaraderie among the musicians.

keyWords.definition: to achieve a victory or success, often after a struggle
keyWords.example: Against all expectations, the small clinic's team triumphed in the research award.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the article?
options: An underdog team's perseverance and camaraderie allow it to triumph despite a long losing streak
A team gives up on handball after a long and disappointing losing streak, and the players go home sad.
A single talented player wins every game for his team without any help from his friends or coach.
A coach decides winning does not matter at all to his players, so he stops the training for the season.
questions.why: The article traces how the Falcons' persistence and growing camaraderie, built during a difficult losing streak, allow them to triumph over the league's strongest team.

wrong.B: The Falcons never give up, despite their losing streak.
wrong.C: Omar scores the final goal, but teamwork is shown driving the team's success.
wrong.D: Coach Faisal cares about effort and teamwork, not about winning being meaningless.

questions.stem: According to the article, how did Coach Faisal respond to the team's repeated losses?
options: He consistently encouraged persistence rather than reacting with anger
He gradually lost interest and stopped attending practice
He blamed individual players for each loss in front of the team
He suggested the team quit handball for an easier sport
questions.why: The article states that Coach Faisal never grew angry about the losses and consistently reminded the team to keep trying and support one another.

wrong.B: Coach Faisal remains actively involved throughout the article.
wrong.C: Coach Faisal is shown encouraging the team, not placing individual blame.
wrong.D: Quitting the sport is never suggested in the article.

questions.stem: What specifically allowed the underdog Falcons to triumph over the previously undefeated Hawks?
options: A lucky bounce of the ball that nobody could control or plan
The Hawks' sudden decision not to compete seriously in the last game
A rule change that favored weaker teams that season in the league
Weeks of accumulated resilience, teamwork, and persistent effort
questions.why: The article attributes the Falcons' eventual triumph to the resilience, camaraderie, and perseverance they built up over many difficult weeks of practice.

wrong.A: The article credits sustained effort, not a lucky bounce.
wrong.B: The Hawks are described as playing their usual strong level.
wrong.C: No rule change is mentioned in the article.

questions.stem: In the article, the word resilience most nearly means —
options: the ability to recover quickly and keep going despite difficulty
a sudden burst of speed late in a game when the team is tired
a formal rule used in handball competitions and school leagues
a type of equipment used during practice by the whole team
questions.why: The article connects resilience to the team's ability to keep practicing and improving despite a long, discouraging losing streak.

wrong.B: Resilience is not about a sudden burst of speed.
wrong.C: Resilience is not a formal competition rule.
wrong.D: Resilience is not a type of equipment.

questions.stem: What can readers infer about why Coach Faisal refused to let the team's confidence collapse?
options: He believed that recovering from losses required steady, patient support, not pressure
He had no real interest in whether the team ever improved, only in the final score
He was required by school rules to stay positive in public, whatever happened
He secretly expected the team to lose every remaining game, but hid it from them
questions.why: Coach Faisal's steady encouragement suggests he understood that lasting resilience comes from patient support rather than pressure or criticism.

wrong.B: His continued encouragement shows real investment in the team.
wrong.C: No school rule about staying positive is mentioned.
wrong.D: His consistent encouragement suggests belief in the team, not resignation.

questions.stem: Which correctly orders these events from the article?
options: The Falcons defeat the Hawks, then begin losing repeatedly at every game
The Falcons' teamwork improves, then they begin losing repeatedly in many games
The Falcons lose repeatedly, their teamwork improves, they defeat the Hawks
The Falcons defeat the Hawks, then their teamwork improves a lot
questions.why: The article describes a long losing streak first, followed by gradually improving teamwork, and finally the decisive win over the Hawks.

wrong.A: The losing streak happens before the win, not after it.
wrong.B: The losing streak comes first, before the teamwork improves.
wrong.D: The teamwork improves before the final win, not afterward.

questions.stem: Why does the author end the article by emphasizing the value of resilience over the single victory itself?
options: To suggest that the lesson of persisting mattered more than any one result
To argue that winning the game was ultimately unimportant to Omar
To explain the official scoring rules of handball in detail
To compare the Falcons' win with a different sport entirely
questions.why: By focusing on resilience and perseverance rather than the scoreline, the author emphasizes that the lasting lesson mattered more than the single win.

wrong.B: Omar clearly feels proud of winning, not indifferent to it.
wrong.C: Scoring rules are not explained in the article.
wrong.D: No other sport is discussed for comparison.

questions.stem: The article suggests that camaraderie mattered as much as skill in the Falcons' turnaround. Which detail best supports this idea?
options: Teammates encouraged whoever made a mistake instead of blaming each other
The Hawks had won every game earlier that season, so the Falcons felt sure they would lose
The match took place during an afternoon practice session, and nobody watched
Omar was the player who scored the winning goal, and the others cheered him
questions.why: Teammates choosing encouragement over blame reflects the camaraderie the article credits for the team's eventual turnaround, alongside improved skill.

wrong.B: The Hawks' record describes the opponent, not the Falcons' camaraderie.
wrong.C: The timing of the match does not relate to camaraderie.
wrong.D: Omar's goal shows the result, not the camaraderie behind it.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says a team that never gives up will eventually succeed, no matter how many times it loses. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the article about the Falcons' resilience and camaraderie.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the article.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I mostly agree that a team that never gives up has a strong chance to eventually succeed. The Falcons lost every game early in the season, yet their resilience and growing camaraderie, built through weeks of patient practice, eventually allowed them to triumph over the undefeated Hawks. Someone might argue that persistence alone cannot guarantee success, since some opponents are simply too strong to beat no matter the effort. However, the article shows that the Falcons' steady improvement in teamwork and skill, not luck, is what finally closed the gap, suggesting that persistence genuinely can change the outcome over time.

LOW.stem: What did Omar do near the end of the game?
options: He passed the ball to Coach Faisal
He sat down and felt sad
He scored a goal for the team
He left the game early

wrong.A: The coach does not play in the game.
wrong.B: Omar was sad earlier, not near the end.

LOW.stem: In the story, the word cheered means —
options: shouted in a happy way
spoke in a quiet way
walked away from the game
cried in a sad way

wrong.B: Cheered loud is not quiet.
wrong.C: Nobody walked away from the win.
wrong.D: Everyone was happy after the win.

LOW.stem: Why did the team get a little better each week?
options: They played a new sport
They had a new coach
The Hawks gave them the ball
They kept coming to practice
LOW.why: The team kept coming to practice, and each week they got a little better at passing and helping.

wrong.A: They kept playing handball.
wrong.B: Coach Faisal stayed their coach.
wrong.C: The Hawks did not help them.

LOW.stem: What did Omar think was most important at the end?
options: Winning every game of the year
That the team never quit
Scoring more goals than anyone
Playing against the Hawks
LOW.why: The story says the team had never quit and that was what mattered most.

wrong.A: The team lost many games, so winning every game is not the point.
wrong.C: The story does not say scoring more goals mattered most.
wrong.D: Playing the Hawks is not called the most important thing.

MID.stem: By how many points did the Falcons beat the Hawks?
options: Two points
Three points
Four points
One point
MID.why: The article says the Falcons won by just one point.

wrong.A: The win was smaller than two points.
wrong.B: The win was smaller than three points.

MID.stem: In the article, the word discouraging means —

easy to understand at once
making you want to quit
very loud and very exciting

MID.stem: What does the author mean by saying that never quitting 'was what mattered the most'?

Practice is not needed by a good team
Omar should score every goal himself

wrong.C: The team practiced every week and improved.

MID.stem: Why does the author begin by asking readers to picture losing every single game?
options: To teach readers the rules of handball
To help readers feel how hard the start was
To show that the Hawks were weak
To explain why Omar loves the coach

HIGH.stem: What did the teammates refuse to do as their camaraderie grew?

Blame one another
Listen to Coach Faisal
Pass the ball to Omar

HIGH.stem: In the article, the word underdog most nearly means —
options: the strongest team in a league
a team that never goes to practice
a team that plays only at home
a team not expected to win
